specFirst: This file was written BEFORE the code (todo/todo-agent-new-theme.md; design in todo/analise-agent-new-theme.md). The code is validated against it. Maintenance changes the spec FIRST, then the code.
description: Standalone agent that GENERATES FROM SCRATCH the current project's theme file (l2/skills/theme.ts, contract v1) via an LLM, guided by the shared themeAuthoring meta-skill, with 2 human checkpoints (clarification). It does NOT clone an existing theme and does NOT improve one (backlog). The theme.ts (plus a deterministic theme.html doc/preview) is written ONLY after the user confirms at the 2nd checkpoint. Consumed downstream by the molecule agents (New Molecule / Variant / Improve), which read the theme to style each molecule's .less.
principles: Generate, don't clone: v1 authors a NEW theme from a natural-language description + clarification answers. Clone (mode A) and Improve Theme (mode C) are backlog.

Human-in-the-loop, lean: exactly 2 checkpoints. Checkpoint 1 collects ONLY the theme fields the initial prompt did not pin down (dynamic questions with options + recommended defaults); if nothing is missing it is skipped (fast path). Checkpoint 2 is a simple confirm (summary + palette; confirm or exit) — NO adjust/iterate loop.
Nothing on disk until confirmed: theme.ts and theme.html are written ONLY on confirm (t4). Everything before lives in l4 draft/artifacts. Exit => discard, nothing written.

Quality is the meta-skill: generation injects l2/aura/molecules/skills/themeAuthoring (the authoring rules distilled from the Variant acceptance tests P3-P10). A generated theme must respect them (geometry is the render's; overlays opaque; primitives not glassified; comments in English; etc.).
Contract-gated: the generated theme.ts must pass the shared validator l2/aura/molecules/shared/vThemeContract.validateVThemeModule before it can be written.

Step is the maintenance unit: 1 folder per step (agent hook, prompt.md when LLM, gate + test, readme, CHANGELOG). helpers/ (nt*) are minimal and owned by this agent; only the theme contract validator is shared.
i18n split: questions/labels/summary are localized (userLanguage detected in t1-plan); the generated theme.ts comments/prose are ALWAYS English (rule P10).

conventions.input: @@agentNewTheme { prompt: '<free description of the desired style, e.g. "a soft neumorphic light theme, brand color #6C5CE7">' } — parsed with mls.common.safeParseArgs. An empty prompt is allowed (all fields fall to Checkpoint 1). Test mode receives JSON { prompt }.
conventions.destinationProject: mls.actualProject (the studio's current project). The theme is written to _<dest>_/l2/skills/theme.ts (+ theme.html).
conventions.admission: The project must NOT already have l2/skills/theme.ts (New Theme creates from scratch). If it exists, fail readable with orientation ('this project already has a theme; Improve Theme is not available yet') — never clobber.
conventions.themeContract: contract v1, validated by l2/aura/molecules/shared/vThemeContract.validateVThemeModule: exports themeInfo{name,suffix(starts with '-'),displayName,description,background{kind:'light'|'dark'|'image',css,note}}, skill (4 sections: '## 1. Visual Signature'/'## 2. Tokens'/'## 3. Canonical CSS Rules'/'## 4. Theme Nuances'(opt)), examples[] (start EMPTY).
conventions.themeFields: Canonical fields collected/derived for the theme: name(->suffix), background.kind(light|dark|image)+css, primary/accent, corners(sharp|rounded|pill), border(none|thin|thick+color), shadow(none|soft|offset), motion(smooth|instant|none), typography(sans|mono|serif + uppercaseLabels?). surface/on-surface(text) are DERIVED from background.kind (light bg -> dark text; dark bg -> light text) and NOT asked. background.kind:'image' is accepted only via free-text CSS (no upload in v1).
conventions.clarification: Human checkpoints use the supported pattern (collab_messages.md 'Rendering a checkpoint'): the step agent EMITS a clarification into its OWN interaction.payload (cheap codefast call returning {type:'clarification', json}); beforeClarificationStep mounts the shared widget; a completed result step '<step>-answer' (which the next step dependsOn) both completes the emitting agent and unlocks downstream. Never a flat clarification in nextSteps; never a wrapper+child. Widgets live in l2/aura/molecules/shared/.
conventions.structuredSummary: t3-generate returns, besides the theme.ts string, a structured summary { name, displayName, background{kind,css}, palette:[{token,label,color}], signature:[{aspect,value}] } persisted to l4. It feeds BOTH the Checkpoint 2 confirmation widget AND the deterministic theme.html.
conventions.writeOnConfirm: theme.ts and theme.html are written to _<dest>_/l2/skills/ ONLY when the user confirms at Checkpoint 2. Exit => discard.
conventions.draft: l4/agentNewTheme/draft.json = { themeTs, summary } produced by t3; l4/agentNewTheme/plan.json = t1 output (known + questions); trace-<step>-<attempt>.json per step.
conventions.gates: 1 gate = 1 file = 1 .test.ts inside the step folder. t3 gate => 1 retry with errors in context; a 2nd failure completes-with-trace (no theme written) and the checkpoint reports it.
conventions.doneAnchors: Every step that passes its gate emits a completed result step with planId 't<N>-done'. Downstream depends ONLY on done anchors. t1 has NO anchor (it is the root's own call — the root plants the tree directly), so on the fast path t3-generate is planted as the first runnable step (waiting_human_input, no dependsOn); with Checkpoint 1 it is planted waiting_dependency on 't2-done'. The Checkpoint 1 answer result IS the 't2-done' anchor (one completed result both completes the emitting step and unlocks t3) — there is no separate 't2-answer'.
conventions.i18n: userLanguage detected in t1-plan drives step titles, questions, labels and the confirmation summary; the theme.ts content is English. The LLM localizes the plan title and the questions; the fixed UI strings (step titles, widget intro/labels) come from a small pt/en table in the code, falling back to English — the t1 schema deliberately has no titles map.
conventions.v2ExplicitlyOut: No clone, no Improve Theme, no image upload, no multi-theme per project, no adjust loop at Checkpoint 2, no smoke-molecule preview. See todo Fase 8.

folderLayout.agentNewTheme.ts: root: parses { prompt }, admission (no existing theme.ts), creates the task (add-message-ai with the cheap t1-plan call), plants the step tree (t2 only when there are questions).
folderLayout.spec.md: human-readable rationale; links to the analysis/control docs
folderLayout.helpers/: ntFs.ts (theme file refs/paths, l4 draft/plan/trace read-write, write theme.ts/.html on confirm), ntSteps.ts (step/intent builders, done anchors, retry policy, clarification plumbing: emit-into-payload + answer result + mutable-parent lookup + apply-intents-and-resume), ntTypes.ts (theme field model + structured summary), ntThemeHtml.ts (deterministic theme.html renderer from the summary)
folderLayout.schemas/: t1-plan.schema.json (plan output: known + questions), t3-generate.schema.json (theme.ts string + structured summary)
folderLayout.steps/t1-plan/: readme.md, prompt.md, gate.ts, gate.test.ts, CHANGELOG.md — NO agent file: the plan call is the ROOT's own message call (see treeOverview), so agentNewTheme.ts owns beforePromptImplicit/afterPromptStep for it. A separate agentNtPlan would cost a second cheap LLM round-trip for the same classification.
folderLayout.steps/t2-clarify/: readme.md, agentNtClarify.ts (emits clarification; mounts Decision Clarification), CHANGELOG.md
folderLayout.steps/t3-generate/: readme.md, agentNtGenerate.ts (LLM design), prompt.md (injects themeAuthoring), gate.ts, gate.test.ts, CHANGELOG.md
folderLayout.steps/t4-confirm/: readme.md, agentNtConfirm.ts (emits confirmation; mounts Theme Confirmation; writes on confirm), CHANGELOG.md

treeOverview: root (t1-plan, cheap LLM: language + admission + known + questions)
-> t3-generate (design LLM: theme.ts + summary, gated, draft only)
-> t4-confirm (CHECKPOINT 2) -> on confirm writes theme.ts + theme.html
strictly sequential; t3 dependsOn t2-done when Checkpoint 1 ran, else t1-done

steps.agentName: agentNewTheme (the root itself — no separate step agent)
steps.goal: Cheap classifier. Admission (project has NO l2/skills/theme.ts; else fail readable). Detect userLanguage + a short title. Parse the initial prompt into `known` (the theme fields it could determine) and build `questions` for the CANONICAL fields still missing (each with options + a recommended default). Persist plan.json. If `questions` is empty, plant t3 directly (fast path, no Checkpoint 1); otherwise plant t2 then t3.

checks: output parses to {known, questions[]} with valid field ids/options
questions never repeat a field or re-ask something already in known
enum options carry enum ids and at most one recommended
gate.onFail: NO retry: fail readable. Admission (no existing theme.ts) is checked EARLIER, in beforePromptImplicit, so it costs no LLM call

steps.doneAnchor: none (the root plants the tree directly)

steps.onlyWhen: plan.questions is non-empty (else this step is not planted — fast path)
steps.goal: CHECKPOINT 1 (collect missing fields). Emit a clarification into this step's own payload; beforeClarificationStep mounts the shared Decision Clarification widget with plan.questions (options + recommended defaults + free-text). On answer, write answers.json to l4 and emit the completed 't2-done' result (the anchor t3-generate dependsOn) carrying the collected values. Cancel => this step fails and the pipeline stops with nothing written.

THE generation call. prompt.md injects the themeAuthoring meta-skill + the initial prompt + `known` + Checkpoint 1 answers. Output via strict tool schema: the COMPLETE theme.ts (string, contract v1, English comments) + a structured summary (name, displayName, background, palette[], signature[]). Persist to l4/agentNewTheme/draft.json. Does NOT write to l2/skills yet.

checks: the generated SOURCE is read statically (parseThemeSource — no eval) and the reconstructed module passes the shared vThemeContract.validateVThemeModule (3 exports, themeInfo fields, suffix starts with '-', 3 mandatory skill sections, examples shape)
raw TypeScript, no markdown fences, no import statements (self-contained data module), skill is one template literal with escaped inner backticks
structured summary present and consistent (name/background identical to themeInfo; palette tokens are --ml-* and declared in the Tokens section)
gate.onFail: retry 1 with gate errors in context; a 2nd failure FAILS the step — nothing is written and t4-confirm never unlocks (a confirmation screen with no theme has nothing to offer; the trace carries the errors)

steps.goal: CHECKPOINT 2 (confirm). Emit a clarification into this step's own payload; beforeClarificationStep mounts the shared Theme Confirmation widget from draft.summary (layout signature + palette swatches). CONFIRM => write _<dest>_/l2/skills/theme.ts and theme.html (deterministic renderer from the summary), compile the .ts best-effort (the molecule agents import the compiled theme.js) and finish. EXIT => discard the draft, write nothing, complete with a 'discarded' trace. Simple confirm — no adjust/iterate loop.

acceptance.regression: none on existing agents beyond the vTheme.ts re-export of the shared validator (agentNewMoleculeVariant suite must stay green)
acceptance.test1: project WITHOUT theme.ts, rich prompt (fast path: no questions) -> generates theme.ts + theme.html on confirm; contract valid
acceptance.test2: project WITHOUT theme.ts, vague prompt -> Checkpoint 1 asks the missing fields with options; answers drive generation
acceptance.test3: Checkpoint 2 EXIT writes nothing; CONFIRM writes both files
acceptance.test4: cycle: run agentNewMoleculeVariant on the freshly created theme (it consumes the new theme.ts) -> a molecule variant is generated
